title: Contributing to ggsaveR
text: anything beyond small fix, please open issue first discuss change. Fork repository create branch. Make change, add tests tests/testthat/ new behaviour bug fixes. Update roxygen comments run devtools::document(). Add bullet top NEWS.md describing change. Check devtools::check() passes without errors, warnings notes. Open pull request.

text: options set, ggsave() must behave exactly like ggplot2::ggsave(). New behaviour switched option, existing scripts need changes. Options validated, invalid values give clear error. Keep hard dependencies minimum; optional features go Suggests.

title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: ggsaveR_options() sets one options, checks , returns previous values can restored: options can set options() prefixing ggsaveR., example options(ggsaveR.formats = c("png", "pdf")). Calling ggsaveR_options() without arguments lists current values.
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf")) getOption("ggsaveR.formats") #> [1] "png" "pdf" options(old)

title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: formats option turns one ggsave() call several files. extension filename replaced format. format can also size, resolution ggsave() arguments. Settings format take precedence arguments given call, arguments call fill whatever format leaves .
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf")) print(ggsave("economy.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)) #> [1] "economy.png" "economy.pdf" options(old) old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(   list(device = "png", width = 180, height = 120, units = "mm", dpi = 300),   list(device = "pdf", width = 180, height = 120, units = "mm") )) print(ggsave("economy.png", p)) #> [1] "economy.png" "economy.pdf" options(old)

what: File names that describe the size
title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: two formats write file, PNG journal PNG slides, ggsaveR adds size names: size one ggplot2 actually uses, scale default dimensions applied. Raster formats also include resolution. size_suffix = TRUE every file gets size suffix; FALSE, clashing names error. format can also carry suffix:
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(   list(device = "png", width = 85, height = 60, units = "mm", dpi = 600),   list(device = "png", width = 254, height = 143, units = "mm", dpi = 150) )) print(ggsave("economy.png", p)) #> [1] "economy_85x60mm_600dpi.png"   "economy_254x143mm_150dpi.png" options(old) old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = list(   list(device = "png", width = 85, height = 60, units = "mm", suffix = "_journal"),   list(device = "png", width = 254, height = 143, units = "mm", suffix = "_slides") )) print(ggsave("economy.png", p, dpi = 150)) #> [1] "economy_journal.png" "economy_slides.png" options(old)

title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: dir places every file saved relative name one folder, created needed. Absolute paths left alone.
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(dir = "figures") print(ggsave("economy.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)) #> [1] "figures/economy.png" options(old)

title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: default existing file overwritten, ggplot2. overwrite_action = "unique", ggsaveR adds number instead: "stop", existing file error. several files saved , check covers anything written, "unique" gives number stay together.
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(overwrite_action = "unique") ggsave("draft.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5) ggsave("draft.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5) #> File exists. Saving to draft-1.png instead. options(old)

title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: guard = TRUE hands call unchanged ggplot2::ggsave(), whatever options set: Scripts use guard need ggsaveR loaded; ggplot2::ggsave() know argument.
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(formats = c("png", "pdf")) ggsave("only-png.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5, guard = TRUE) options(old)

title: Getting started with ggsaveR
text: ggsaveR attaches ggplot2 loaded, ggsave() takes precedence whichever package loaded first. ggplot2::ggsave() always reaches original.

title: Reproducible figures: embedded data and logging
text: embed_data = TRUE, every PNG file carries expression passed plot, data behind plot, printed sessionInfo() plot object. information stored file’s text chunks, image looks opens viewer. read_ggsaveR_data() reads information back: plot stored variable, ggsave("plot.png", p), recorded expression just p. data plot object embedded either way.
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(embed_data = TRUE)  ggsave(   "versicolor-virginica.png",   iris |>     subset(Species != "setosa") |>     ggplot(aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, colour = Species)) +     geom_point(),   width = 6, height = 4 ) #> Embedded reproducibility data into versicolor-virginica.png (140.9 Kb) options(old) info <- read_ggsaveR_data("versicolor-virginica.png") #> 'versicolor-virginica.png' also holds the plot object. Use `trusted = TRUE` to restore it, but only if you trust the file. cat(info$plot_call) #> ggplot(subset(iris, Species != "setosa"), aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length,  #>     colour = Species)) + geom_point() head(info$plot_data) #>   Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width    Species #> 1          7.0         3.2          4.7         1.4 versicolor #> 2          6.4         3.2          4.5         1.5 versicolor #> 3          6.9         3.1          4.9         1.5 versicolor #> 4          5.5         2.3          4.0         1.3 versicolor #> 5          6.5         2.8          4.6         1.5 versicolor #> 6          5.7         2.8          4.5         1.3 versicolor

text: creator option stores name Author field PNG files, file managers image viewers can display:
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(creator = "Jane Doe, University of Somewhere") ggsave("signed.png", restored, width = 6, height = 4) options(old)

title: Reproducible figures: embedded data and logging
text: log option appends row CSV file every file saved, including variants. MD5 checksum shows whether figure manuscript still matches one script produced.
code: old <- ggsaveR_options(log = "figures-log.csv", formats = c("png", "pdf"))  p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point() ggsave("weight.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5) ggsave("weight-smooth.png", p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x),        width = 5, height = 3.5) options(old)  read.csv("figures-log.csv")[, c("file", "device", "width", "height", "dpi", "plot")] #>                file device width height dpi #> 1        weight.png    png     5    3.5 300 #> 2        weight.pdf    pdf     5    3.5  NA #> 3 weight-smooth.png    png     5    3.5 300 #> 4 weight-smooth.pdf    pdf     5    3.5  NA #>                                              plot #> 1                                               p #> 2                                               p #> 3 p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) #> 4 p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)

what: A Wrapper for ggplot2::ggsave with Extra Features
title: A Wrapper for ggplot2::ggsave with Extra Features
text: ggsaveR provides drop-replacement ggplot2::ggsave() whose extra behaviour set , global options, instead every call. Add two lines top existing analysis script every ggsave() call : save figure several formats sizes, consistent file names; write figures one folder, never overwrite existing file; produce greyscale colour vision deficiency versions, can check colour palette works every reader; embed code, data R session PNG files, figure can traced back produced ; record every saved file, size checksum, CSV log. options set, ggsaveR::ggsave() behaves exactly like ggplot2::ggsave().
